newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY BOND DEMAND SLUMPS DUE TO CBANK RATES - AKK.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY BOND DEMAND SLUMPS DUE TO CBANK RATES - AKK.

text.p: Hungary's three-year government bonds were substantially undersubscribed at an auction on Thursday due to the effect of a recent central bank rate hike, the Government Debt Management Agency (AKK) said.
Less than eight percent of the offered bonds, worth 40 billion forints, were subscribed at the auction at an average yield of 17.36 percent.
"The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) raised (its six-month deposit) rate recently, and this probably rebounded here," AKK deputy director Laszlo Borbely told Reuters.
"The market judged that the reachable maximum yield on the paper was too low."

The NBH's move on March 24 to raise the six-month deposit facility rate to 21.00 percent from 20.75, aimed at protecting savings, shocked markets which had been saturated with repo rate cut expectations after three months of decline in rates.

The rate hike was followed by a rise in interest rates at government securities auctions and on the secondary market, and created some tension between the state budget, interested in cutting its interest rate costs, and the NBH, dealers said earlier this week.
They predicted that the tension was probably behind substantial undersubscription at the three-year bond auction as the yield on the bonds was low even compared with other government securities.
Borbely said undersubscription at government bond auctions was unprecedented this year but AKK was not surprised by the low demand at Thursday's auction.
He also confirmed that there was disagreement between the AKK and the NBH concerning their interest rate policies.

"There is a dispute between us and the NBH, and it's not yet over," he said, adding that the AKK and the central bank would continue regular weekly discussions. "We would like to wait until next week's discount Treasury bill auctions before saying anything."
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said following the NBH rate hike that his relations with the central bank and its president Gyorgy Suranyi remained good.
He added that the central bank's aim with rate hike was to stabilise the markets in the short term, but he added interest rates would continue the declining trend later this year.
The government plans to reduce average inflation to some 17 percent this year, while a recent Reuters survey of 15 analysts showed forecasts for 1997 averaging 18.39 percent.
Analysts said earlier that year-on-year inflation, currently 18.8 percent, may not decline further in the second and third quarters of this year but was likely to drop later.
Borbely said the undersubscription at the auction would not cause financing problems for the state budget, even though substantial stocks of government papers would mature next week.
"We have reserves for tough times like this," he said. "This does not cause a financing problem."
Seven-year government bonds worth 10 billion forints were a shade oversubscribed at a second auction on Thursday.

Dealers predicted earlier this week that part of the potential demand for three-year bonds was likely to pass to the seven-year auction as the yield of seven-year bonds, offering three percent coupon over inflation, was considered better.
